title: Stale-range guard checks only the start line, so a grown symbol body is silently under-read
body: All four prompts (design.md:47, design-scout.md:32, discovery-lite.md:22, discovery.md:38) say: read a file's line_ranges first, and read the whole file only if `symbol` is not on the `start` line. The trace is built at intake, and discovery/design can run much later, after other merges. The most common kind of staleness is lines added or removed INSIDE the function body or below its def line. In that case the name is still on `start`, the guard passes, and `end` points into the middle of the function (or past it). An agent following the wording literally reads a truncated function. The wording also never says that the ranges are a starting point: they are capped at 3 per file, and the build log shows 97.5% of read-slice files get ranges. So 'read ranges first' may be taken as 'ranges are enough'. AC-9 asked only for the start-line check, so the code meets the letter of the AC. The concern is prompt wording that encourages agents to under-read, which is in this review's scope.
fix: Add half a sentence to the shared wording: 'ranges are an entry point, not a limit; if the block does not visibly close at `end` (the next line is still indented body, or the range cuts a statement), keep reading to the end of the block or read the whole file.' Keep the wording identical in all four prompts and regenerate klc-plugin/.

title: The primary AC-6 sort key (IDF weight descending) is not pinned by any test
body: Verified by mutation. I changed `keep = sorted(best, key=lambda k: (-best[k], k[2], ...))` to `(best[k], k[2], ...)` in planning-retriever.py:264, which ranks the RAREST match LAST. All 39 runnable klc137 tests still passed. The four tests that did not run need git; they check only structural properties (keys, <=3 entries, start<=end, name on the start line) and not order. The ordering test's own docstring says every candidate ties on IDF weight ('widget' is their only shared token), so only the `start` tiebreak is covered. The IDF ordering matters because it decides which 3 symbols survive the cap, so a regression here silently changes what agents are pointed at. By contrast, a mutation that dropped `_capped_symbol_names` WAS caught by the wide25 test.
fix: Add a fixture file with more than 3 query-matching symbols whose best tokens have DIFFERENT IDF weights (e.g. one symbol carries a token that is unique in the corpus, others share a common one). Assert the exact kept list, with the rare-token symbol first even though its `start` is later.

title: New crash path: a non-dict element in inventory `symbols` now raises AttributeError from build_trace
body: `_symbols_by_file_name` calls `s.get(...)` on every element that `inv_symbols` returns. `inv_symbols` validates only that `symbols` is a list, not what each element is. Verified: with the real 'base' fixture views plus `inv['symbols'].append(1)`, the post-ticket `build_trace` raises `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'get'`. The pre-ticket retriever (58b44d91) on the same input returns status 'ok'. A non-string `name` (e.g. a list) would likewise raise TypeError, because it is used in the hashed `(file, name)` key. This contradicts the docstring ('degrades exactly like every other optional inventory read in this module'). `planning_validate` guards the same loop with `isinstance(s, dict)`. The deterministic builder never emits such elements, so the risk is limited to hand-edited or corrupted inventories.
fix: In `_symbols_by_file_name`, skip `s` unless `isinstance(s, dict)` and `isinstance(s.get('file'), str)` and `isinstance(s.get('name'), str)`. Add one malformed-element case to the emission tests.

title: Python ranges start at the `def`/`class` line and exclude decorators; the prompts do not say so
body: Per AC-1, `line` equals ast `lineno`, which for a decorated definition is the `def` line. A real build over a fixture confirmed that the functools.lru_cache decorator and the staticmethod decorator above `def decorated` and the property decorator above a method sit outside `[start, end]`. Decorators often carry behaviour an agent needs for planning: caching, routes, `pytest.mark.parametrize` data, the property decorator. An agent that reads only the range misses them. The data is correct per the spec; the gap is in the reading instruction.
fix: In the shared prompt sentence, add 'also read the few lines above `start` (decorators/attributes)', or document the decorator exclusion next to `line_end` in docs/architecture.md.

title: Module docstring still shows the pre-ticket symbol shape without `line_end`
body: The docstring says the frozen schema is stated once, in `core.shared.inventory`, but it still carries an inline copy: `{"name": str, "kind": str, "file": str, "line": int, "sig": ...}`. That copy now disagrees with `SYMBOL_FIELDS` and with core/agents/inventory.md, which both gained `line_end`. This is exactly the two-documents drift the KLC-103 note warns about.
fix: Add `"line_end": int | None` to the docstring example, or delete the inline copy and keep only the pointer to `CANONICAL_SCHEMA`.

title: AC-13 tests split lines with str.splitlines(), which disagrees with ast-grep/ast numbering on files containing U+2028/U+0085/\x0c; a missing `line_ranges` key is silently skipped
body: Both real-substrate tests (this file and test_klc137_real_substrate_inventory.py) index lines with `read_text().splitlines()`. `str.splitlines()` also splits on U+2028, U+0085, \x0c and similar characters, but ast-grep, Python ast and editors count only \n. Verified on the tracked file tests/test_klc139_skeleton_review_fixes.py: ast-grep and ast both put `def test_header_line_count_matches_ast_not_splitlines` on line 131, while `splitlines()[130]` is ')' and the def lands at index 131, i.e. line 132. core/ has no such file today, so both tests pass. But any stored ticket query that ranks that test file into the read slice would fail the 'symbol on start line' assertion for a correct range. Separately, `if line_ranges is None: continue` carries the comment 'checked below', but nothing below checks it. A trace that lost the `line_ranges` key entirely would pass, as long as some other trace is non-empty.
fix: Split with `text.split('\n')` (or `io.open(newline='')` + split on '\n') in both tests. Replace the `None` skip with `assert 'line_ranges' in trace`.
